question: Has this already been made, published or claimed?

usc102.cite: 35 U.S.C. § 102: Conditions for patentability; novelty. United States Code.
usc102.checked: subsections (a) and (b)(1) read word for word on the Cornell Legal Information Institute page on 20 Nov 2026

epc.cite: European Patent Convention, Articles 54 (Novelty) and 56 (Inventive step). European Patent Office, 2020 text.
epc.checked: Articles 54 and 56 read word for word on the EPO's pages (a54.html, a56.html) on 20 Nov 2026

steps.title: Search everywhere
steps.text: Prior art is anything the public could get at, not only papers. Search patents, standards, products, catalogues, theses and talks.

quotes.text: The state of the art shall be held to comprise everything made available to the public by means of a written or oral description, by use, or in any other way
patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public

steps.title: Check the date
steps.text: Only what was public before your filing date counts. US law excuses some of the inventor's own disclosures made up to a year before.

quotes.text: before the effective filing date of the claimed invention
A disclosure made 1 year or less before the effective filing date of a claimed invention shall not be prior art to the claimed invention under subsection (a)(1) if

steps.title: Is it new?
steps.text: Compare your idea with each earlier source, feature by feature. If one source already shows it, it is not new.

quotes.text: An invention shall be considered to be new if it does not form part of the state of the art.

steps.title: Is it obvious?
steps.text: Even if no single source shows it, ask whether a skilled person would have combined what was known to get there.

quotes.text: An invention shall be considered as involving an inventive step if, having regard to the state of the art, it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art.

limits: The page quotes the law, not a search guideline: how patent offices actually search (classification codes, EPO Guidelines for Examination) is not covered here.
"Feature by feature" in step 3 is our summary of how novelty is judged; the statutes quoted do not spell it out.
In re Hall (1986), the card's example, was not read for this page.
Outside patent law, a prior art review for a paper or a design uses the same idea of what was public first, without the legal tests.
